answer: Bind standing to an apprenticeship chain. A newcomer joins a master who sets a task, checks it against a mirror session log, then passes the apprentice through twelve masters, each taking one apprentice per epoch, gating the next stage. Each handoff earns a lotus mark; the apprentice must keep one ember project, a tool, alive through all twelve stages, or the chain restarts. One identity costs twelve supervised stages over a year; ten thousand fakes would need 120,000 master slots from a pool of 3,000, assigned by lottery, never sold, so bulk buying adds no slots and no stage can be skipped.
